name: SMC Global Securities Ltd
title: SMC Global Securities Ltd - 543263 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q4 revenue +22.6% YoY and EBITDA margin 17.4% (+250bp) on broking and insurance leverage, but FY26 EBITDA fell 10.3% and PAT 29.9% as NBFC AUM shrank to INR 1,119 crore and finance costs rose to INR 221.3 crore.

evasions.quote: So, there would be minimal impact or rather very negligible impact or maybe no impact on our operations.

summary.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated operating income rose 22.6% YoY to INR 516.9 crore and PAT to INR 21.5 crore, while FY26 PAT fell 29.9% to INR 103.2 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 recovered sharply year on year across all three segments, with consolidated EBITDA of INR 89.7 crore (margin 17.4%, up 250 bps YoY) and PAT of INR 21.5 crore versus INR 4.1 crore in Q4 FY25. Sequentially, EBITDA and PAT moderated on the March 2026 market correction, a technical disruption and seasonality. For full-year FY26, consolidated income grew 5.7% but EBITDA fell 10.3% and PAT fell 29.9%, driven by higher finance costs (INR 221.3 crore) and a deliberate slowdown in the NBFC lending book. Management framed FY26 as a transition year and said it expects to rebuild return metrics in FY27.

financial_highlights.change: +42.4% to 42.6% YoY (figure differs between speakers); margin +250 bps YoY
vs INR 4.1 crore in Q4 FY25; PAT margin 4.2%, +320 bps QoQ
vs INR 13.92 in FY25; not like-for-like as paid-up capital rose from INR 20.9 crore to INR 41.9 crore

segments.name: Broking, Distribution and Trading
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 19.3% YoY to INR 286.8 crore and segment EBIT rose 66.6% YoY to INR 60.9 crore. FY26 revenue grew 4.3% to INR 1,089.2 crore while EBIT was INR 239.4 crore (down about 3%). Online penetration reached 72% (from 61%), client base 13.39 lakh, broking DP AUA INR 1,42,703 crore (+23.96%), MF AUM INR 4,294 crore.

segments.name: Insurance Broking
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 29.8% YoY to INR 208.1 crore with segment EBIT of INR 4.5 crore (+6.7%). FY26 revenue grew 17.1% to INR 667.5 crore, EBIT grew only 4.8% to INR 14.3 crore on investment in distribution and technology. Gross premium INR 3,145 crore; 11.39 lakh policies issued; upgraded to composite broker.

segments.name: Financing (NBFC)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 segment revenue rose 6% YoY to INR 43.3 crore and EBIT rose 18.6% to INR 21.2 crore. FY26 revenue fell 15.1% to INR 188.9 crore, EBIT fell 26.2% to INR 102.2 crore and PAT fell to INR 24.6 crore from INR 46.3 crore. AUM INR 1,119 crore (vs INR 1,291 crore); disbursements INR 720.05 crore; NIM 7.3% (from 8.2%).

guidance_outlook: NBFC AUM expected to grow 15-20% in FY27, with stronger growth from new product lines expected from FY28-29.
Insurance broking revenue expected to grow about 15% in the next financial year, helped by the reinsurance segment.
Management expects a gradual rise in commodity share of broking revenue (currently about 10%, up from 4-5%).
Non-SME disbursements (excluding LAP and unsecured business loans) expected to rise from INR 614 crore to above INR 800 crore.
Management expects to return to a more measured growth posture in financing as macro and credit conditions stabilise, and to progressively rebuild return metrics in FY27.
capex_capacity: Network of 203 branches across 396 cities; financing business operates through 38 branches in 7 states.
Insurance workforce of 503 employees, 16,610 agents and 393 motor insurance service providers.
Upgrade from direct broker to composite broker enables entry into reinsurance; investment in distribution capacity and technology is ongoing.
Stoxkart opened 100,000 clients in FY26 and is ranked fourth by active clients on NSE for FY26 (per management).
demand_pricing: Derivatives volumes moderated during FY26 under higher STT on F&O, phased true-to-label charges and the F&O participation framework; management is shifting focus to cash, delivery, distribution and advisory.
Broking revenue mix (per Ajay Garg): cash about 50%, F&O about 40%, commodity about 10%, up from 4-5% earlier.
Stoxkart revenue grew 150% in FY26 (per Pranay Aggarwal).
Monthly SIP sourcing of about 1,900-2,000 SIPs; live SIPs 94,392 at average INR 2,722 (about INR 25.69 crore per month).
Insurance cross-sell: more than INR 8 crore of premium sourced via broking network in FY26, all offline; online cross-sell being built into the mobile app.
NBFC asset quality: GNPA 3%, NNPA 1.99%, credit cost 1.3%, collection efficiency 98.63%, secured AUM 76.71%.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of broking revenue across cash, F&O and commodity, and whether commodity spiked?
qa_highlights.answer: Ajay Garg said the split is about 50% cash, 40% F&O and 10% commodity; commodity was 4-5% earlier and is now 10%, with expected gradual growth as new products such as electricity contracts launch.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NBFC disbursements fall and what is the product outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Himanshu Gupta said LAP disbursements fell from INR 70 crore in FY25 to negligible, unsecured business loans fell from INR 281 crore to INR 93 crore, and other products grew from INR 452 crore to INR 614 crore; AUM growth of 15-20% is targeted.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the RBI circular on leverage for propriety trading?
qa_highlights.answer: D. K. Aggarwal said arbitrage is deployed from surplus treasury funds, the company is sufficiently capitalised, and impact is expected to be negligible.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the GNPA level and when will disbursements recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Himanshu Gupta said GNPA is about flat YoY but above FY24 because of a few large secured accounts in legal or settlement process, with adequate provisions made; disbursement growth is expected from the non-LAP, non-unsecured book.

qa_highlights.question: What growth is expected in insurance broking given digital aggregator competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Sakshi Mehta expects about 15% growth next financial year, with reinsurance contributing and both physical and digital selling pursued; general insurance is about 90% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What NCD borrowing was raised and why?
qa_highlights.answer: Himanshu Gupta said the NBFC raised about INR 25 crore of fresh NCDs and the broking entity about INR 150 crore, to diversify away from bank borrowing. Bank borrowings were 85% of the NBFC mix in FY26 versus 79% in FY25.

risks_watch: Finance costs (INR 221.3 crore) and NBFC NIM compression (7.3% vs 8.2%) continue to pressure consolidated margins.
Recovery of large secured GNPA accounts that are in legal or settlement process.
RBI directions on bank exposure to capital market intermediaries and on leverage for NBFC and group entities in proprietary trading; management says impact is minimal.
Derivatives volume and regulatory cost headwinds (STT, true-to-label charges) affecting broking revenue.
Competition from large digital aggregators in insurance broking.
Reconciling the EBITDA growth figure for Q4 (42.6% in the opening remarks vs 42.4% in the CFO remarks).
summary.management_tone: Confident on the Q4 recovery and the fee-based businesses, but openly transparent and defensive about the FY26 NBFC slowdown and margin compression. Answers on disbursement and GNPA were detailed but leaned on product-level reasoning, and some answers on proprietary trading and funding were brief.
key_quotes: This was a conscious choice, not a constraint.
We want to be transparent with our investors that FY26 our margin compressed at the consolidated level on a full-year basis.
We believe diversified, well-capitalized intermediaries with strong compliance frameworks are best placed in this evolving environment.

adds.what: Upgrade from direct broker to composite broker enabling reinsurance entry (no capacity number given)

growth.why: Management guides NBFC AUM growth of 15-20% and insurance broking revenue growth of about 15% in FY27, with non-LAP SME disbursements above INR 800 crore, but backing is partial: the NBFC lending book shrank to INR 1,119 crore from 1,291 crore, and reinsurance entry is not sized.
